subject: Student Perspectives on Racism and Equity
overview: Hosts Danielle Balocca and Chelli Keshavan interviewed three students from the Brooks Elementary School CCSR about anti-racism and racial equity. The discussion focused on why understanding race is necessary for students and how to transition from being a bystander to an upstander when witnessing discrimination.

items.title: Introduction of CCSR Student Guests
items.summary: Danielle Balocca introduced Kyden Cabrales, Martin Alvanos, and Caleb Davis, three students from a CCSR subgroup focused on anti-racism and Black Lives Matter.

items.title: Importance of Discussing Race
items.summary: The students explained that discussing race is important for navigating future life experiences and identifying how to help peers who face bullying.

items.title: Historical Context and Systemic Racism
items.summary: Participants discussed skin color differences and how historical laws regarding segregation and slavery continue to influence modern economic and social disparities.

items.title: Equity, Equality, and Black Lives Matter
items.summary: The group utilized analogies involving firefighters and medical aid to distinguish between equality and equity in the context of racial justice movements.

items.title: Bystander Intervention and Being an Upstander
items.summary: Students described the importance of being an 'upstander' by reporting racism to adults and not allowing silence to validate a bully's behavior.

items.title: Final Takeaways on Addressing Racism
items.summary: The conversation concluded with the students emphasizing that racism is unacceptable and can be addressed through protests and public dialogue.
